tonight.headline: Four Jaguars in one lineup, all playing the same game at Denver
body: Week 2 has not started. ESPN has this at 117.6 KEI returns to your 114.7, a 49% coin flip. Your lineup is already set correctly — you swapped Trevor Lawrence in over Stafford at 07:18 this morning, which was the standing call, so there is no lineup card today.

The thing worth seeing is not a projection. Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Cam Little and the Jaguars defence are all in your starting nine and all four play the same game at Denver. Roughly 37 of your projected points ride on one afternoon in Colorado going well.

case.label: What the stack means
case.body: Correlation cuts both ways and the downside is sharper than the upside here, because the defence and the kicker pull against the quarterback. A Jacksonville blowout win gives you Lawrence and Little and the defence. A 44.5-point game that Denver control at 2.5-point favourites gives you very little from any of the four.

case.label: Why it is not fixable today
case.body: Fixing it means a waiver claim, and IPADE priority never resets — one claim drops you to last for the season. The strategy file is explicit that priority is for a player who starts immediately or wins a league, never for a streamer or a hedge. Nothing on the wire clears that bar this week, so the stack stays.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Team 13 trade landing. Lamar Jackson replacing Lawrence in the starting slot cuts the Jacksonville exposure from four starters to three and removes the highest-variance one. That is a second reason to send it that has nothing to do with the point maths.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — but send it today, they have all week to think
doFirst.title: Send Team 13 the Golden-for-Lamar Jackson offer
doFirst.subtitle: They roster two quarterbacks in a one-QB league and start Travis Kelce in their flex. This fixes both of them.

case.label: The structural surplus
case.body: Team 13 start Josh Allen at slot 0 — 366.5 for the season and not what you are asking for — and carry Lamar Jackson at 312.9 on their bench, where he scores them nothing every week. Their flex is Travis Kelce at 178.1 because no third receiver clears him: DeVonta Smith and DJ Moore start, and Xavier Worthy sits at 173.9, four points short. Matthew Golden at 190.3 clears Kelce and unlocks the slot.

case.label: What you are buying
case.body: A quarterback who went 17 of 25 for 324 and two touchdowns in a 41-23 Week 1 win. Checked properly again this morning: a search on Jackson's health surfaces a Ravens knee-soreness report dated November 2025, which is a year old, not this season, and is not being used.

case.label: Verified on this morning's snapshot
case.body: You go 2054.0 to 2080.5, +26.5. They go 1969.9 to 1982.1, +12.2. Both sides gain and theirs is the larger single-position upgrade. Their slot column was re-read this morning and is unchanged: Allen starting, Jackson benched, Kelce in the flex.

case.label: The second reason, which is not in the maths
case.body: It breaks the Jacksonville stack. Lawrence, Tuten, Little and the defence all play at Denver on Sunday. Jackson in the starting quarterback slot takes a quarter of your projected points out of that one game.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They trade or drop one quarterback, acquire a third receiver who clears Kelce, or Golden's price rises past what the flex gap is worth to them. Worthy at 173.9 is already closer to Kelce than he was — if they work that out themselves, the offer loses most of its appeal to them.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · decide after Friday's injury report, not Wednesday's
doFirst.title: Do not drop Michael Mayer yet — Bowers is day-to-day, not back
doFirst.subtitle: The trigger written on Sunday has not fired. Hold one more read.

case.label: Where the thesis stands
case.body: Mayer was added for the Brock Bowers vacuum and the log already closed that thesis WRONG when Schefter reported Bowers could return in Week 2. The drop was then reversed in timing, not direction, on the reasoning that a Week 3 return leaves Mayer one more startable week in a flex that takes tight ends.

case.label: What today's reporting says
case.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has Bowers day-to-day after the knee procedure: 'We're gonna be smart with him, but if he's ready to play, he's gonna play.' That is neither a return nor a ruling out. Las Vegas play the Chargers and Mayer took six catches for 32 yards in Week 1 with Bowers off the field.

case.label: Why the drop is not free
case.body: IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so a second startable tight end has real value here in a way it never does in Chem. Mayer at 85.0 is the lowest season projection on your roster and that is a projection argument; the reporting points the other way for one more week, and there is no claim you want to make with the seat anyway, because priority never resets.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Bowers practises in full on Wednesday or carries no designation on Friday — then Mayer is the drop before Sunday. If Bowers is limited or sits Wednesday, keep Mayer through Week 2 and read it again next Monday. Either way the decision point is Friday, not tomorrow morning.

action.label: Drop Michael Mayer — only if Bowers clears Friday

whatWentWrong.title: Bowers moved again, and the Mayer drop you were told to make on Wednesday is now a Friday decision
whatWentWrong.lead: Sunday said Week 2 return. Monday said Week 3. Today says day-to-day with no timeline.

case.label: The three readings in three days
case.body: Schefter had the Raiders believing Bowers might miss only one game. Dr Deepak Chona, reading the same meniscus trim, put a two-week ramp as possible with Week 3 more likely. Kubiak now has him day-to-day and will play him if he is ready. Three credible sources, three different answers, and no practice report yet to separate them.

case.label: What it costs you
case.body: Almost nothing, and that is the point worth keeping. Nothing on this roster was droppable when the first version of this card was written, so no action was foregone. The error was writing a Wednesday trigger for a question Wednesday cannot answer.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Friday's designation. A full Wednesday practice or a clean Friday sheet retires Mayer; anything less keeps him. Stop re-reading it in between.

whatWentWrong.title: Team 13's bench now has a third receiver, and it narrows the trade you are about to send
whatWentWrong.lead: Xavier Worthy at 173.9 is four points off Travis Kelce. The offer's appeal to them rests on that gap.

case.label: The margin
case.body: The offer works because Matthew Golden at 190.3 clears Kelce's 178.1 in their RB/WR/TE flex and unlocks 12.2 season points. Worthy sitting at 173.9 means they are already most of the way there on their own bench. The +12.2 is real but it is not the runaway it reads as.

case.label: Why it still goes out today
case.body: The quarterback half is not marginal. Lamar Jackson scores them nothing on a bench in a one-QB league behind Josh Allen, every week, all season. That is the part of the trade that should sell it, and the copy text leads with it rather than with the flex.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They start Worthy in the flex before answering, which says they have found the four points themselves and no longer need Golden. Watch their lineup, not their inbox.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +12.2 and it is the cleaner half of the deal — they are converting a quarterback who scores them nothing behind Josh Allen into the flex starter they do not currently have. Say that first.

case.label: Why they are paying for nothing
case.body: One-quarterback league. Josh Allen starts at 366.5. Lamar Jackson sits at 312.9 on their bench and returns them zero every single week. That is the definition of structural surplus and it is the thing to trade into.

case.label: What it fixes for them
case.body: Their flex is Travis Kelce at 178.1 because no receiver on the roster clears him — Smith and Moore start, Worthy is 173.9. Golden at 190.3 goes straight into that slot. Their optimal lineup rises 1969.9 to 1982.1.

case.label: What it fixes for you
case.body: You go 2054.0 to 2080.5. You also stop starting a quarterback in the same game as your kicker, your defence and your flex back — four Jaguars at Denver on Sunday is roughly 37 projected points on one afternoon.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Jackson was checked this morning, not carried: 17 of 25 for 324 and two touchdowns in a 41-23 Week 1 win, and the only injury item a search returns is Ravens knee soreness dated November 2025 — a year old and not used. The real risk is that this is priced on seasonProj, which has not moved in fifteen hours across a full week of football and may be a preseason field.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They trade or drop one quarterback, start Xavier Worthy in the flex, or acquire a third receiver. Any of those and the offer stops being worth anything to them.

trades.copyText: Hi — you've got Lamar Jackson sitting behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he's scoring you nothing every week. I'll give you Matthew Golden for him. Golden (190.3 rest-of-season) goes straight into your flex over Travis Kelce (178.1), which is about +12 season points for you and turns a dead bench QB into a starter. I get the QB upgrade, you get the slot you can't currently fill. Fair both ways — interested?

worthALook.name: Jalen Coker
worthALook.lead: The best player on this wire, and in this league he is a watch rather than a claim. That is the priority rule doing its job.

case.label: Why he is the best player available
case.body: 8 catches on 9 targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 — 36.8 points, the top-scoring receiver in the NFL. He rolled an ankle in the first quarter, was photographed in a boot Monday, and told reporters it was precautionary and he expects to practise Wednesday. Ownership is rising and he is 50.9% rostered nationally.

case.label: Why you are not claiming him
case.body: IPADE priority never resets. One claim puts you last for the rest of the season, and you are currently 5th of 10. The standing rule is that priority buys a player who starts immediately or wins a league — and Coker would not start here. Your two receiver slots are Rashee Rice and Garrett Wilson, and the flex has Tuten in it. He would be a bench stash bought with a season-long asset.

case.label: The asymmetry, stated plainly
case.body: He is being claimed in Chem this morning, where priority resets weekly and the claim is free. Same player, same evidence, opposite answer, and the only variable is the waiver rule. That is the whole reason the two leagues get separate briefs.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Garrett Wilson or Rashee Rice goes down, or if Coker posts a second week above 25 points and is still unrostered here, he stops being a bench stash and becomes a starter — and a starter is what priority is for. Until one of those happens, watch him.

worthALook.sources: NBC Sports · DraftKings Network · Yahoo Sports

worthALook.name: Ravens D/ST
worthALook.lead: 2nd for Week 2, hosting New Orleans, 89.9% rostered nationally and free here. Still not worth your priority.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: Lindy's Week 2 board has Baltimore 2nd and Jacksonville 9th. Baltimore is rostered in nine of every ten leagues and sits unclaimed in this one. On the evidence this is the single largest ownership anomaly on your wire.

case.label: The number that stops it
case.body: Baltimore 2nd against Jacksonville 9th is worth perhaps two points this week. Priority here is a one-time, season-long asset. Spending it on a two-point defence upgrade is precisely what the strategy file forbids — never a bye-week patch, never a handcuff, never a streamer.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Never for a defence, as things stand. If Baltimore is still sitting there in Week 7, when Jacksonville's bye takes your defence, kicker and flex out together, the calculus changes — because then it is not a stream, it is filling three holes at once. That is the week to look, not this one.

doNotChase.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
doNotChase.lead: Yesterday's watch row in the other league called him Jacksonville's goal-line back. The Week 1 tape says otherwise, and the correction applies here too.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six touches to Tuten's 16, 41% of snaps to 48%, and one red-zone carry — which was the only red-zone carry any Jacksonville back got in the game. Sports Illustrated's Week 1 review has him 'relegated to short-yardage duty'.

case.label: Why he is worse than that here specifically
case.body: You already own Tuten. Adding his short-yardage partner is buying more of the same Denver game you are already over-exposed to, in a full-PPR league where a back with no receiving role collects the least valuable touches available.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten missing time. Then Rodriguez is a genuine handcuff and worth a free-agent add — check the status field first, because a free agent costs no priority and a waiver claim costs all of it.

doNotChase.name: Tyler Loop
doNotChase.lead: K2 this week against your K8. The kicker slot is where this roster has already burned two moves for nothing.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Loop K2, Cam Little K8. Six places, worth under a point. Little returned 12.0 in Week 1 and is the highest-projected kicker available to this roster at 146.1 for the season. This is not a hole.

case.label: The pattern
case.body: The log carries this exact slot going Little to Boswell on 8 September and Boswell back to Little on 10 September — two moves in two days with no stated reason either way. It came out right on the week and was still recorded as CHURN, because being right about an unreasoned reversal is luck. A third move on six ranking places, paid for with permanent waiver priority, would be the worst version of it yet.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Little finishing outside the top 20 kickers across Weeks 2-4, which is the falsification condition already on the record for the hold. Even then, a free agent yes; a waiver claim no.

cannotSee.label: Priority is a one-shot asset and I cannot see what it is worth later
cannotSee.body: Every claim recommendation in this league is really a bet about the rest of the season. I can price Coker and Baltimore this week; I cannot price the injury in Week 9 that you will wish you still had priority for. The rule that priority buys only an immediate starter is a rule precisely because that future is unknowable.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only returns your own. Coker is 50.9% rostered and rising, and one of the other nine managers may take him at 07:00 UTC — in which case this brief's advice not to spend priority on him becomes free of charge rather than a decision.

cannotSee.label: seasonProj has not moved across a full week of football
cannotSee.body: The Team 13 trade recomputes to exactly yesterday's numbers — 2054.0 to 2080.5 and 1969.9 to 1982.1, to the decimal, fifteen hours later. The Chem trade does the same. That is consistent with seasonProj being a static preseason field, which would mean both trades are priced on August's opinion rather than on anything Week 1 revealed. It is the single largest unverified assumption in this brief.

cannotSee.label: Most defence grades are dashed and none of them are guesses
cannotSee.body: Only three positional or unit-level reads were retrievable this morning: Detroit against quarterbacks, the Week 2 D/ST board and the Week 2 kicker board. For Kansas City against backs, Tennessee against backs, Green Bay against receivers and Minnesota against tight ends, no source returned a number, so Taylor, Barkley, Garrett Wilson and Loveland carry no grade rather than an invented one.

cannotSee.label: MarShawn Lloyd's Week 1 usage was never confirmed
cannotSee.body: Josh Jacobs being on the commissioner's exempt list indefinitely is well sourced, and so is the expectation that Lloyd takes roughly twenty touches a game. His actual Week 1 snap share is not — the Packers.com piece that came back in search was dated August. That is why Tuten keeps the flex and Lloyd is a bench note, and it is the call in this brief most likely to be wrong.

cannotSee.label: The Texans defence is still unresearched, so the alternate trade shape is still unpublished
cannotSee.body: Team 13 carry two defences and start the weaker one — Seahawks 126.5 at slot 16, Texans 132.6 on the bench. Golden for the Texans D/ST is a second shape worth asking about if they decline Lamar Jackson. It is not in the trades section for the second day running because no search was spent on the Houston defence, and no player gets named without one.
